name: Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP)
description: Examines the absolute confidence level mathematically assigned by the language model to its chosen words. AI models consistently output words where the 'Softmax' probability distribution is heavily skewed toward a single, overwhelmingly preferred candidate. Human writing exhibits far more variance, frequently utilizing words with much lower predictive certainty.
mechanism: At the final layer of any Large Language Model, a 'Softmax' function converts raw mathematical scores (logits) into a probability distribution across the entire vocabulary, summing to 1.0 (100%). When an AI generates text (assuming standard temperature settings), the 'Maximum Softmax Probability' (the probability of the single word it actually chooses) is extremely high—often approaching 0.90 to 0.99 for grammatical connectors and predictable nouns. The AI is highly 'confident' in its choices because it is following mathematical optimization. Human writers, however, frequently select words that an LLM's Softmax function would assign a relatively low probability to (e.g., 0.15 or 0.05), because humans prioritize creative nuance or specific memory recall over statistical likelihood. By passing the target text through a reference model and calculating the average Maximum Softmax Probability for every token, this method detects the telltale 'overconfidence' signature of algorithmic generation. A text maintaining an unbroken chain of 90%+ softmax probability scores is mathematically impossible to have been written organically by a human.
useCase: Highly effective for detecting AI-generated news articles, academic abstracts, and marketing copy where the AI naturally falls into highly predictable, high-confidence phrasing patterns.
strengths:
• Bypasses basic paraphrasing; slightly reorganizing a sentence doesn't change the fact that the underlying word sequence consists entirely of high-probability tokens.
• Very strong white-box diagnostic metric when analyzing text against the exact model suspected of generating it.
• Mathematically rigorous and highly interpretable as a continuous confidence score.
limitations:
• Requires access to a robust reference language model to calculate the Softmax distributions, making it computationally heavy.
• Can be defeated if a user aggressively manipulates the 'Top-P' (Nucleus Sampling) and 'Temperature' parameters during generation, forcing the AI to select lower-probability tokens.
• Highly rigid, formulaic human writing (e.g., legal contracts) is inherently predictable and can yield high MSP scores, causing false positives.
parameters:
Analysis: Per-Token Logit-to-Softmax Distribution Scoring
Metric: Average and Variance of Maximum Softmax Probabilities
Output: 0-100 Algorithmic Confidence (Predictability) Score
accuracy: High — 82-89% on standard generative texts. It provides a foundational statistical bedrock for AI detection that is difficult to camouflage without making the text incoherent.

references.title: Hendrycks, D. & Gimpel, K. (2017). A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples. ICLR.
Solaiman, I. et al. (2019). Release Strategies and the Social Impacts of Language Models. arXiv.
